newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CFO sees Q4 stock buyback completion.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CFO sees Q4 stock buyback completion.

text.p: Chrysler Chief Financial officer Gary Valade said he expects the automaker to complete its $2 billion 1996 stock buyback program during the fourth quarter.
In a conference call, Valade told reporters that the automaker had about $400 million worth of stock to complete its planned share repurchases.
Chrysler repurchased about 15.8 million shares at a cost of $452 million during the third quarter of 1996. So far this year, the automaker has bouught back 51.9 million shares for $1.57 billion.
Under terms of Chrysler's standstill agreement with investor Kirk Kerkorian, the automaker has committed to buying back another $1 billion worth of shares in 1997.
Chrysler shares were trading up 1 to 32-3/4 following the company's announcement that its third quarter profits nearly doubled to $680 million from $354 in the same period of 1995.

Chrysler's net operating profit, excluding a $55 million charge for early retirement costs, came to $735 million, or $1.00 per fully diluted share, well ahead of the First Call consensus estimate of $0.69 a share.
